talks.title: Welcome | Simon Bennetts & Scott Gerlach | ZAPCon 2022
talks.teaser: Investigates welcome | Simon Bennetts & Scott Gerlach | ZAPCon 2022 and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Overview: Scott Gerlach of StackHawk MCs ZAPCon 2022's opening session with Simon Bennetts, welcoming the global OWASP ZAP community to the second annual virtual application security testing conference.

Key Topics: ZAPCon as community conference for OWASP ZAP users and contributors; global timezone-inclusive scheduling across Asia, Europe, and Pacific regions; recorded talk replays for missed sessions; and application security testing best practices with ZAP.

Technical Details: Gerlach outlines the conference schedule, Discord engagement expectations, and replay availability for attendees across multiple timezones who cannot watch live due to scheduling conflicts or meetings.

Takeaways: ZAPCon demonstrates how open-source security tools build thriving global communities. Virtual formats with on-demand replays enable worldwide participation in practitioner-focused security events.

talks.title: ZAP for Everybody | Venkata Subrahmanyam & Ved Mishra | ZAPCon 2022
talks.teaser: Presents ZAP for Everybody | Venkata Subrahmanyam & Ved Mishra | ZAPCon 2022 and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Overview:
Venkata Subrahmanyam and Ved Mishra, security engineers at Goldman Sachs, present their experience scaling dynamic application security testing (DAST) across hundreds of enterprise applications using OWASP ZAP. The talk outlines their internal framework, known as Project ARIES, which orchestrates headless OWASP ZAP scanners within Kubernetes and GitLab CI/CD pipelines. The presenters discuss overcoming operational hurdles associated with automated authentication, API schema ingestion, and vulnerability triaging at enterprise scale.

Key Topics:
- Scaling OWASP ZAP dynamic application scanning across hundreds of repositories
- Headless architecture and containerized execution inside Kubernetes clusters
- Automated authentication workflows and API endpoint enumeration (OpenAPI/Swagger)
- Integrating DAST findings into centralized data lakes and automated Jira ticketing

Technical Details:
The speakers explain that commercial web vulnerability scanners often struggle with the custom authentication frameworks, complex single-page architectures, and high deployment velocities characteristic of enterprise software pipelines. To address these constraints, Goldman Sachs developed ARIES, a wrapper around the open-source OWASP ZAP engine. Instead of relying on ZAP's graphical interface, ARIES runs headless ZAP instances inside lightweight Docker containers scheduled across elastic Kubernetes pods, allowing dozens of application scans to execute simultaneously without resource contention.

ARIES automates the complete scanning lifecycle through configuration files defined alongside source code in GitLab repositories. The platform dynamically ingests OpenAPI, Swagger, and GraphQL schemas to ensure deep coverage of backend microservices. Authentication is managed through modular script hooks that simulate single-sign-on (SSO) login flows, acquire JWT bearer tokens, and maintain valid session cookies throughout automated active scanning passes. Scan outputs are automatically deduplicated, correlated against asset inventories, and streamed into an enterprise data lake, triggering automated Jira tickets for verified high-severity vulnerabilities.

Key Takeaways:
Open-source security tooling like OWASP ZAP can match or exceed commercial DAST capabilities when wrapped in cloud-native orchestration frameworks. Successful automated dynamic scanning hinges on reliable session management and structured API schema parsing rather than generic web spidering. Security teams should integrate DAST scans directly into CI/CD pipelines with clearly defined severity policies to catch runtime security flaws before production release.

talks.title: Kick-Off | Joni Klippert | ZAPCon 2022
talks.teaser: Evaluates kick-Off | Joni Klippert | ZAPCon 2022 and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Welcome and ZAP overview

StackHawk CEO Joni Klippert opens ZAPCon 2022, welcoming attendees on behalf of ZAP creator Simon Bennetts and the community. She describes OWASP ZAP as the widely used open-source DAST engine for modern apps, APIs, and automation—StackHawk's product is built on it.

DevOps AppSec shift

Klippert argues cloud-first microservices, CI/CD, and API-centric SPAs require modern DAST with API testing. ZAPCon sessions cover automation, GitHub Actions workshops, OAuth top 10, and practitioner panels on leveling up AppSec.

Community growth

ZAPCon 2021 exceeded 2,300 registrants versus a 400-person goal, prompting the 2022 return with doubled content and hands-on workshops. StackHawk announces a $100,000 ZAP community fund for contributions and thanks core maintainers Simon, Ricardo, Rick, and Axton plus sponsors Snyk and CircleCI.

talks.title: The OWASP Top Ten 2021 and ZAP | Jim Manico | ZAPCon 2022
talks.teaser: Reviews the OWASP Top Ten 2021 and ZAP | Jim Manico | ZAPCon 2022 and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
## OWASP Top 10 as a Teaching Framework

Jim Manico's ZAPCon 2022 keynote walks the OWASP Top Ten 2021 at speed, linking each category to practical secure-development guidance and showing where OWASP ZAP helps automate discovery.

## Access Control and ZAP

For broken access control—the #1 risk—Manico stresses that scanners cannot know your authorization policy. ZAP's access-control testing add-on lets teams encode application-specific rules so automated tests reflect real business logic, not generic guesses.

## Injection Still Dominates

Despite decades of awareness, injection (including XSS merged into the category) remains pervasive. Manico reminds developers that validation alone cannot fix SQL injection; parameterized queries and safe APIs are the durable fix, not regex filters on exotic inputs.

## Resources and Mindset

He points attendees to OWASP cheat sheets, NIST SP 800-162 for attribute-based access control, and ASVS requirements. The through-line: combine ZAP automation with human policy knowledge to close gaps that turnkey scans alone will always miss.
